entry: Form of solid atmospheric precipitation, made of balls or irregular lumps of ice called hailstones. Hail is distinct from ice pellets, though the two are often confused. Hailstones usually measure between 5 mm (0.2 in) and 15 cm (6 in) in diameter. They form in the strong upward air currents of [[Cumulonimbus cloud|cumulonimbus clouds]], growing layer by layer as they are carried up and down, and they fall faster as they grow. Hail is most frequent in mid-latitude continental regions such as the central United States, while in the tropics it tends to be confined to high elevations. Hail causes serious damage to property and, most commonly, to [[Crop|crops]]. Severe weather warnings are issued when stones reach a damaging size, which the U.S. National Weather Service sets at 1 in (2.5 cm) in diameter.

Ethiopian former long-distance runner and businessman. He won two Olympic gold medals and four World Championship titles in the 10,000 metres, taking that event at the 1993, 1995, 1997 and 1999 World Championships. He won the [[Marathon|marathon]] in [[Berlin|Berlin]] on four consecutive occasions between 2006 and 2009. At the 2008 Berlin Marathon he ran a world record time of 2:03:59, breaking his own world record by 27 seconds. He set 27 world records in total and broke 61 Ethiopian national records. In 2021, during the [[Tigray war|Tigray War]], he pledged to join the fighting against the Tigray People's Liberation Front. He is also a successful businessman, and New African cited him as one of the top 100 most influential Africans in 2011.

Emperor of Ethiopia (r. 1930–1974). He served as regent under Empress Zewditu from 1916 to 1930. He introduced reforms including the 1931 constitution and the abolition of slavery in 1942. He led the empire during the [[Second Italo-Ethiopian War|Second Italo-Ethiopian War]] and, after its defeat, was exiled to the United Kingdom. In 1963 he presided over the formation of the Organisation of African Unity, the precursor of the [[African Union|African Union]], and served as its first chairman. He was overthrown in the 1974 coup by the [[Derg|Derg]], a military junta, and in 1994 the Derg was revealed to have assassinated him. Among adherents of [[Rastafari|Rastafari]] he is called the returned Jesus, although he was himself an adherent of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Critics, including Human Rights Watch, describe his administration as autocratic, while others fault Ethiopia's slow modernization.

Southernmost province of China, comprising Hainan Island and smaller islands in the South China Sea. The island was part of [[Guangdong|Guangdong]] from 1950 to 1988, when it became a province of its own. Designated a special economic zone by [[Deng Xiaoping|Deng Xiaoping]] under the [[Reform and opening up|reform and opening up]] program, it is now a centre of tourism. The Han Chinese form 82% of the population, and the Hlai, an indigenous Kra–Dai-speaking people, about 15%. Haikou, on the northern coast, is the capital, and Sanya is a well-known resort on the southern coast. China administers the disputed Spratly and Paracel Islands under Sansha city, while many of the Spratly Islands are controlled by [[Vietnam|Vietnam]] and the [[Philippines|Philippines]]. In 2020 the government announced a plan to make the island the Hainan Free Trade Port, aiming to make it the largest free-trade port in the world by 2035.

Third-largest city in Vietnam, on the Gulf of Tonkin (pop., 2025: 4,664,124). Centrally governed, Haiphong (*Hải Phòng*) covers 3,194.72 sq km, including Bạch Long Vĩ and Cát Bà islands. It was the first city in Vietnam and Mainland Southeast Asia to be electrified. After three French soldiers died in a clash there, French ships shelled the city, precipitating the [[First Indochina War|First Indochina War]]. During the [[Vietnam War|Vietnam War]], U.S. Navy and Air Force aircraft bombed the city, and on May 8, 1972, Admiral Thomas H. Moorer ordered the mining of its harbor, effectively sealing the port. In February 2025 the parliament approved an $8 billion investment to upgrade the French-built Kunming–Haiphong railway under the [[Belt and Road Initiative|Belt and Road initiative]]. In June 2025 Hải Dương Province was merged into Haiphong.

Styling of hair, usually on the human head. Hairstyles may alter the length, texture, shape or arrangement of hair. They are part of personal grooming and [[Fashion|fashion]], though practical, cultural and popular considerations also shape them. The oldest known depiction of hair styling is hair braiding, which dates back about 30,000 years. Hairstyles are markers of social class, age, marital status, racial identification, political beliefs and attitudes about gender. Some people cover their hair for cultural or religious reasons, such as women in Islam who wear the [[Hijab|hijab]], married women in [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi Judaism]] who wear the sheitel or tichel, and men and women in [[Sikhism|Sikhism]] who wear the dastar. In the [[Roman Empire|Roman Empire]], noblewomen's hairstyles grew so complex that they required daily attention from several enslaved people and a stylist.

Country in the Caribbean, on the western side of the island of Hispaniola. The capital and largest city is [[Port-au-Prince|Port-au-Prince]]. The Taíno were the Indigenous inhabitants, and in 1492 [[Christopher Columbus|Christopher Columbus]] established the first European settlement in the Americas on its northeastern coast. The western part of the island became French Saint-Domingue, dominated by sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans. The [[Haitian Revolution|Haitian Revolution]] (1791–1804) made Haiti the first sovereign state in the Caribbean and the first country in the Americas to abolish slavery. U.S. forces occupied the country from 1915 to 1934, and the Duvalier family ruled as dictators from 1957 to 1986. A coup in 2004 was followed by a [[United Nations|United Nations]] intervention. Gang activity has displaced more than 1.3 million people, and the presidency has been vacant since the assassination of Jovenel Moïse in July 2021.

Slave revolt and war of independence in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, 1791–1804. Its leaders included [[Toussaint Louverture|Toussaint Louverture]], a former enslaved man who emerged as the most prominent general. The revolt began on August 21, 1791, and the colony became independent as Haiti on January 1, 1804. It is one of the only known slave rebellions to lead to a state free from slavery, though not from forced labour, and ruled by former enslaved people. It was the largest slave uprising since [[Spartacus|Spartacus]]'s revolt against the [[Roman Republic|Roman Republic]] nearly 1,900 years earlier. The revolution reshaped debates over slavery, strengthened the abolitionist cause and sparked revolts in nearby colonies. France did not officially recognize Haiti's independence until 1825, and Haiti was required to pay an indemnity of 150 million francs, a heavy financial burden.

African diasporic religion that developed in Haiti between the 16th and 19th centuries. It arose through [[Syncretism|syncretism]] between traditional religions of West and Central Africa and [[Catholic Church|Catholicism]], and it absorbed influences from [[Freemasonry|Freemasonry]]. Vodou has no central authority. It teaches a creator divinity, Bondye, and spirits called lwa, who are equated with Catholic saints. Followers seek the lwa's aid through offerings, [[Divination|divination]] and ceremonies in which dancers are possessed by a lwa. Vodouists are initiated into temples run by a *oungan* (priest) or *manbo* (priestess). Many Vodouists took part in the [[Haitian Revolution|Haitian Revolution]], after which the Catholic Church left for several decades and Vodou became Haiti's dominant religion. Most Haitians practice both Vodou and Catholicism. The religion has been described as one of the world's most misunderstood.

Annual Islamic pilgrimage to [[Mecca|Mecca]], Saudi Arabia. It is one of the [[Five Pillars of Islam|Five Pillars of Islam]], a duty required once in a lifetime of Muslims who are physically and financially able to make the journey. The rites take five to six days, from the 8th to the 12th or 13th of Dhu'l-Hijja, the last month of the lunar [[Islamic calendar|Islamic calendar]], so their Gregorian dates shift each year. Pilgrims wear white garments (*ihram*), circle the [[Kaaba|Kaaba]] seven times, walk between the hills of Safa and Marwah, stand in vigil at Mount Arafat, and stone three pillars representing the Devil. Official statistics for 2000 to 2019 give an average of 2,269,145 attendees per year. In June 2020 Saudi Arabia admitted only a very limited number of pilgrims, all residents of the country, because of the [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]].

Nigerian-American former basketball player, nicknamed the Dream. Born in [[Lagos|Lagos]], he played 18 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association|National Basketball Association]], primarily with the Houston Rockets. Drafted first overall in 1984, he led the Rockets to back-to-back championships in 1994 and 1995, and was named NBA MVP in 1994. That season he also won Defensive Player of the Year and Finals MVP, and he remains the only player in NBA history to win all three in one season. He retired as the league's all-time leader in blocks, with 3,830, and was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2008.

Language group of Chinese varieties spoken by the Hakka people in southern China, Taiwan and overseas communities. The varieties are not mutually intelligible with Yue, Wu, Min or Mandarin, and Hakka is most closely related to Gan. Its varieties are spoken in [[Guangdong|Guangdong]], [[Fujian|Fujian]], [[Hainan|Hainan]], and in [[Taiwan|Taiwan]], [[Singapore|Singapore]], [[Malaysia|Malaysia]], [[Thailand|Thailand]] and [[Indonesia|Indonesia]]. The name literally means guest families. The Hakka trace their origins to migrations from North China during periods of war and unrest, as far back as the end of the Western Jin (266–316). Taiwan designates Hakka as one of its national languages. The Meixian dialect of northeast Guangdong has been taken as the standard by the government of mainland China.

Collective body of Jewish religious law, derived from the [[Torah|Written and Oral Torah]]. Halakha is based on biblical commandments, [[Talmud|Talmudic]] and rabbinic law, and customs compiled in works such as the Shulchan Aruch and the Mishneh Torah. Often translated as Jewish law, a more literal rendering is the way one proceeds. Halakha guides religious practice and belief, as well as many aspects of daily life. In the diaspora it served many Jewish communities as an enforceable law, both civil and religious. According to the Talmud, the Torah contains 613 mitzvot, 248 positive and 365 negative, supplemented by seven mitzvot legislated by rabbis of antiquity. Because halakha is developed by various authorities rather than one official voice, communities may give different answers to halakhic questions.

Arabic term for what is permissible under [[Sharia|Islamic law]]. Although the term is often associated with dietary laws, particularly the slaughter of meat, halal also governs business and finance, such as the prohibition of usury (riba), and daily living. In the [[Quran|Quran]], halal is contrasted with [[Haram|haram]], meaning forbidden. Islam generally considers all food halal unless it is specifically prohibited in the Quran or [[Hadith|hadith]], and pork is the only meat that is categorically forbidden. Halal has grown into a global industry, with certification bodies serving the food, pharmaceutical, [[Cosmetics|cosmetic]] and financial sectors. The halal economy has grown especially in countries with large Muslim populations, such as Malaysia, Indonesia and the [[Middle East|Middle East]].

2004 first-person shooter video game by [[Valve Corporation|Valve]]. The sequel to *Half-Life*, it was released for Microsoft Windows on November 16, 2004, through [[Steam (service)|Steam]]. It follows Gordon Freeman in a resistance against the alien Combine empire. Built on Valve's Source engine, it added detailed physics simulation and a gravity gun. Development took five years and cost $40 million. The game received acclaim and numerous Game of the Year awards, and it was ported to Xbox, Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, macOS and Linux. By 2011 it had sold 12 million copies. It was followed by the episodic sequels *Episode One* (2006) and *Episode Two* (2007).

1998 first-person shooter video game developed by [[Valve Corporation|Valve]], its debut product, published by Sierra Studios for Windows. The player controls Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist who must escape the Black Mesa Research Facility after a disastrous experiment brings aliens into it. The story is told through scripted sequences rather than cutscenes. The game runs on GoldSrc, a modified version of the Quake engine. It won more than 50 PC Game of the Year awards and had sold more than nine million copies by 2008. The sequel *Half-Life 2* followed in 2004.

Time required for a quantity to reduce to half its initial value, symbol t½. Commonly used in nuclear physics to describe how quickly unstable atoms undergo [[Radioactive decay|radioactive decay]], the term also applies to any exponential decay, such as the biological half-life of drugs. [[Ernest Rutherford|Ernest Rutherford]] discovered the principle in 1907 and used it to date rocks by the decay of [[Radium|radium]] to lead-206. For a radioactive atom, half-life is defined in terms of probability: on average, exactly half of the entities decay in that time.

Maritime disaster in [[Halifax, Nova Scotia|Halifax]], Nova Scotia, on December 6, 1917. The French cargo ship SS *Mont-Blanc*, loaded with high explosives, collided at low speed with the Norwegian vessel SS *Imo* in the harbour. Benzol barrels on the French ship's deck leaked and were ignited by sparks, and about 20 minutes later *Mont-Blanc* exploded, devastating the Richmond district. At least 1,782 people were killed and an estimated 9,000 injured. The blast released energy equivalent to roughly 2.9 kilotons of [[TNT|TNT]]. A [[Tsunami|tsunami]] created by the blast wiped out a Mi'kmaq community in the Tufts Cove area.

Capital and most populous municipality of [[Nova Scotia|Nova Scotia]], Canada (pop., 2025: 544,834, metropolitan area). The municipality was formed in 1996 by amalgamating Halifax, Dartmouth, Bedford and Halifax County. It is the economic centre of Atlantic Canada, with major employers including the Department of National Defence, Dalhousie University, Saint Mary's University, the Halifax Shipyard and the Port of Halifax. Before 1749 Nova Scotia was administered from Annapolis Royal. That year Governor Edward Cornwallis founded Halifax, named for George Montagu-Dunk, 2nd Earl of Halifax, on a site the Mi'kmaq called Chebucto. In the 2021 census, 348,634 people lived in the municipality's [[Urban area|urban area]].

American pop rock duo, formed in Philadelphia in 1970. Daryl Hall sang lead while John Oates played electric guitar and sang backing vocals. They achieved their greatest fame from the mid-1970s to the late 1980s, fusing rock, soul and rhythm and blues. Of their 33 singles, 29 charted on the Billboard Hot 100 between 1974 and 1991, and six reached number one, including "Rich Girl" and "Maneater". The duo was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2014. In April 2024 Oates indicated that the duo would no longer perform together, amid a legal battle between them.

Voltage produced across a conductor, transverse to a current flowing in it and to a magnetic field applied perpendicular to the current. Edwin Hall discovered the effect in 1879 while working on his doctoral degree at [[Johns Hopkins University|Johns Hopkins University]] in [[Baltimore|Baltimore]], [[Maryland|Maryland]]. Eighteen years before the electron was discovered, his measurements confirmed [[James Clerk Maxwell|James Clerk Maxwell's]] electromagnetic theory. Charge carriers moving in a magnetic field experience the [[Lorentz force|Lorentz force]], which pushes them to one face of the conductor. The resulting electric field opposes further migration of charge, so a steady voltage is established.

American actress and producer. She won the Miss Ohio USA title in 1986 and was first runner-up at Miss USA that year. She produced and starred in the television film *Introducing Dorothy Dandridge* (1999), which won her a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award. She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her role in *Monster's Ball* (2001). Her other roles include Storm in the *X-Men* film series (2000–2014), Jinx in *Die Another Day* (2002) and the title role in *Catwoman* (2004). In 2020 she made her directorial debut with the [[Netflix|Netflix]] drama *Bruised*.

Song by [[Leonard Cohen|Leonard Cohen]], released on his 1984 album *Various Positions*. The album was rejected by [[Columbia Records|Columbia Records]], and the song achieved little initial success. Its popularity grew after John Cale recorded a version in 1991, and it was featured in the 2001 film *Shrek*. Jeff Buckley's 1994 recording, inspired by Cale's version, was ranked 259th on [[Rolling Stone|Rolling Stone]]'s list of the 500 Greatest Songs of All Time in 2004. By 2008 more than 300 versions were known. The song re-entered the Billboard Hot 100 for the first time after Cohen's death.

Short-period comet visible to the naked eye from Earth, officially designated 1P/Halley. It returns every 74 to 79 years, last appearing in 1986 and next due in mid-2061. Its returns were recorded from at least 240 BC, but in 1705 the English astronomer [[Edmond Halley|Edmond Halley]] used [[Isaac Newton|Isaac Newton]]'s laws of gravity to show that several sightings were of the same comet. In 1986 the [[European Space Agency|European Space Agency]]'s [[Giotto|Giotto]] mission became the first spacecraft to observe a comet in detail. Its results supported Fred Whipple's "dirty snowball" model, which predicted that the comet would be a mixture of volatile ices and dust. They also showed that the surface is largely dusty, non-volatile material, with only a small portion of it icy.

1978 American slasher film directed and scored by [[John Carpenter|John Carpenter]]. [[Jamie Lee Curtis|Jamie Lee Curtis]], in her film debut, stars as Laurie Strode, a teenager stalked on Halloween by Michael Myers, who had murdered his sister at the age of six. [[Donald Pleasence|Donald Pleasence]] plays the psychiatrist Dr. Samuel Loomis, who pursues him. Shot in Southern California on a low budget, the film grossed $70 million. Many critics credit it with pioneering the [[Slasher film|slasher]] genre, alongside *Psycho* (1960). It was selected for preservation in the National Film Registry in 2006, and it spawned a franchise of thirteen films.
